decision.question: QA1 runtime topology: modular monolith versus containers
decision.sensitivity: 218 deterministic runs (16 weight +-50%, 200 seeded random weight vectors, unknown pessimistic/optimistic bounds); zero winner flips

probes.A_unsafe_split: REJECTED - violates frozen hard constraints (gateway-only effects, single canonical state owner) regardless of latency score
probes.B_incomplete_monolith: REJECTED as INCOMPLETE - no declared failure boundary or deterministic replay interface

decision.migration_trigger: split only when a measurable trigger fires (load beyond the single-process S1-002 envelope, an availability-domain requirement, or a new trust boundary); the split starts with the state container (single-writer canonical state + transactional outbox inside it), never with policy caches or async audit
decision.non_goals: no production Docker/Kubernetes deployment, no orchestrator/cloud vendor choice, no production availability claims, no core runtime changes, no SQLite/Postgres or execution backend replacement

limitations: Boundary measurements are same-host and bounded; multi-host partition semantics and orchestrator restart latencies are unknown and excluded from scoring (bounded in sensitivity S3).
The recommendation is a research decision for the MVP; it is not a production deployment, availability, or reliability claim.
S1-002 and S1-004 evidence is PASS_WITH_LIMITS and is reused only within its stated limits.
Producer and verifier labels are process-separated roles in one local environment, not external human auditors.
The containers restart/recovery cell remains unknown until a bounded container prototype is measured (production deployments are out of scope for this ticket).
note: research-plan PASS_WITH_LIMITS is a research evaluation; it never sets Goal ACCEPTED (release gate only)
